patch.value: Spanish (es) locale for package-owned UI strings

Add a Spanish (es) locale catalog for the package-owned SPA UI strings (auth, nav, banners, settings, consent, dialog, error mapping). Register es in locale resolution and the settings language selector (English/Deutsch/Espanol). Legal pages remain an operator concern and are not translated by this package.

es.json catalog exists with all 110 en keys translated to natural Spanish (usted register); es registered in SUPPORTED_LOCALES and resolveLocale (es and es-MX prefix match); settings language selector offers English/Deutsch/Espanol; npm run typecheck && npm run build && npm test green; catalog-parity test covers es automatically
Work completed and released in 2026.7.18. Release attribution set explicitly so pm-changelog --respect-item-release files the entry under 2026.7.18 instead of the current release notes.
A closed item whose changelog entry appears under the 2026.7.18 heading it actually shipped in, leaving the current release notes untouched.
Item remained in_progress with no activity after its work shipped, so the delivery was absent from the changelog while still counting as open work in every fleet audit.

Retired as shipped: the Spanish locale, shipped as public/src/i18n/es.json was completed and released in 2026.7.18, but the item was never closed and sat in progress ever since, inflating every fleet audit.

value.author: claude-code
value.text: Release attribution corrected to 2026.7.17-1 after review. The first attribution used the item's last-activity DATE, which is unsound: an item can be touched before the release that finally carried its code. Verified instead by tag containment — git tag --contains c46797f reports 2026.7.17-1 as the first release holding the implementation commit. Greptile caught this on PR #67 by noticing a historical release predating its implementation.

patch.value: Before this closeout the item had remained in_progress with no activity since its work shipped, so the delivery was missing from the changelog while still being counted as open work in every fleet audit. Closing it with an explicit release attribution is what added the historical entry.
